messages:
infra-oncall: seeing a sudden surge of GPU pods Pending in us-west-2-gpu pool, autoscaler is scaling but new nodes never become Ready :fire:
infra-oncall: logs show a lot of 'InstanceLaunchFailed: subnet IP allocation' and kubelet timeouts
infra-oncall: tagging for incident response, cc @mira @kai @ash

mira: on it, pulling scheduler events
mira: scheduler reports '0/120 nodes are available: 120 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu' for many pods but nodes show GPU capacity in node groups

kai: can you paste a sample pod event?
mira: "FailedScheduling: 0/24 nodes are available: 24 Insufficient free addresses for podIPs"

ash: that looks like ENI / subnet IP exhaustion not GPU shortage. Recent churn in nodepool might have fragmented ENI assignments
ash: also seeing cluster-autoscaler 1.24 logs: 'scale up rejected: nodegroup max size reached' then later 'scale up ok' then scale down attempts -> oscillation

lenna: any recent infra changes in us-west-2? subnet CIDR changes?
ops-lead: we rolled an infra template yesterday that tightened ENI limits for that nodegroup (to mitigate IP-per-node ballooning). Might have been too aggressive.

infra-oncall: autoscaler-bot: report for nodegroup us-west-2-gpu-spot
autoscaler-bot: ActivePods: 134, DesiredNodes: 32, CurrentNodes: 12, MaxNodes: 32, UnreadyNodes: 5
autoscaler-bot: Recent events: provisioning stuck due to "AttachNetworkInterface: No available addresses"

mira: scheduler backlog is piling, lots of retries from a cronjob that launched 200 short-lived GPU pods in parallel (cron misconfig)
mira: looks like a runaway job from repo/tooling 'eval-batch-runner' with backoff disabled

kai: putting quick mitigations: 1) pause the cron, 2) create a PriorityClass and requeue only critical pods, 3) cordon spot nodegroup to force dedicated pool fallback

ash: commands I ran: 
```
kubectl -n infra patch cronjob eval-batch-runner -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'
kubectl create priorityclass emergency-high --value=100000 --global-default=false
kubectl label nodes -l nodepool=us-west-2-gpu-spot node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable=true
kubectl drain node/<hot-node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

lenna: paused cron succeeded, backlog stopped creating new pods. But many Pending pods still queued and autoscaler still hitting ENI errors

ops-lead: temporary network mitigation: requested cloud team to increase subnet secondary IP quota and expand CIDR for nodepool (ticket #CLOUD-4821)

mira: in the short term we can: 1) reschedule some pods to a different AZ with available ENIs, 2) create a fallback nodepool in the same cluster with different subnet (non-overlapping), 3) set cluster-autoscaler --max-graceful-termination for stability

kai: created fallback nodepool us-west-2-gpu-fallback on different subnet and scaled to 8 nodes as emergency: `terraform apply` completed, nodes are joining now

autoscaler-bot: New nodes from us-west-2-gpu-fallback reporting: 6 Ready, 2 NotReady (kubelet start), attaching ENIs OK

infra-oncall: re-labelled critical pods with nodeSelector to point to fallback nodepool for high-priority workloads. Low-priority eval batch pods remain Pending until quota release

ash: noticing one issue: autoscaler still sees many unready nodes in original pool and triggers scale up/scale down loops because max_unready not configured. Suggest setting `--max-total-unready-percentage=20` and `--scale-down-unneeded-time` higher temporarily

lenna: applied patch to cluster-autoscaler flags via k8s Deployment patch. Monitoring for 5m

ops-lead: cloud quota request approved to add 256 secondary IPs to the subnet; once that propagates provision should stabilize. ETA ~15m

mira: pod scheduling improvement visible, pending count dropping from 340 -> 68 in 10m. GPU job queue priority working

infra-oncall: follow-ups: - revert cron change once safe - audit cronjob retry/backoff and add rate-limits - update infra template ENI limits and subnet sizing - add autoscaler flags to defaults - add alert when subnet free-ip < 20%

ops-lead: agreed. creating post-incident ticket with remediation steps and cost estimate for fallback nodes (we used 8 emergency nodes, ~12 node-hours)

kai: nice quick containment team. Recommend a runbook update for 'subnet ip exhaustion' with commands we used and steps to create fallback nodepool

mira: adding runbook draft to /docs/runbooks/networking-subnet-ip-exhaustion.md and will link in ticket

infra-oncall: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring for stabilization. Will keep channel open until 1h stable. :white_check_mark:
